_meta.note: Named targets for verify.py, postman.py and the console: python verify.py --env <name>. SECRETS DO NOT BELONG HERE. Any value may be written as ${VAR} and is resolved from the shell, from .env, or from environments.local.json — both of which are gitignored. This file holds the shape of an environment and is safe to commit.

auth_modes.none: send nothing (the mock, unless started with --require-auth)
auth_modes.token: a token you already have: {mode, token, header?, prefix?}
auth_modes.login: call a login endpoint: {mode, path, method?, send: query|json|form, username_field?, password_field?, username, password, token_path?, use_cookies?}

_meta.setup: cp environments.local.example.json environments.local.json and put real credentials there, or export the variables in your shell / CI secret store.
_meta.data: Per-environment test data. A suite's `data` says what a value MEANS; an environment's `data` says what it IS on that server — the id of a row that exists on staging is not the id of one on dev. Merged over the suite's own data at run time, and --var beats both. ${VAR} works here too, so an id that is sensitive stays out of git.

mock.description: The local mock. Nothing to authenticate against unless it was started with --require-auth.

mock-auth.description: The local mock started with --require-auth, for exercising 401 handling.

mock-login.description: The local mock, driven through the real login flow — proves an environment's login config before you point it at dev.
